content: GAIL (India) Limited is recognized as the largest natural gas transportation company in India, encompassing all components of the natural gas value chain. The company, originally known as Gas Authority of India Ltd, serves as the primary entity for gas transmission and marketing in India. It was established by the Government of India in August 1984 with the objective of developing infrastructure for the gas sector. In 1991, GAIL successfully commissioned the 2,800-kilometer Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur (HVJ) pipeline, a significant milestone in its operations. Between 1991 and 1993, the company constructed three LPG plants and acquired several regional pipelines, which facilitated the initiation of gas transportation services across various regions of India. In 1997, GAIL ventured into city gas distribution in New Delhi by establishing nine compressed natural gas (CNG) stations. Subsequently, in 1999, the company established northern India’s sole petrochemical plant in Pata. In 2007, GAIL was recognized by Forbes as one of the 2,000 largest public companies globally.
